verses.verse:
पंचमस्तु द्विधा प्रोक्तः स्वयं भूतश्च कृत्रिमः।
स्वाभाविके त्वनिर्वाहे क्रियते कृत्रिमः स्वरः।४६।
verses.text: Pa is said to be of two kinds, svayaṃbhūta (self-born) and kṛtrima (artificial); when the natural one cannot be managed, the artificial note is made.

commentary.text: This baddha pañcama (bound Pa) has other advantages too. For example, if after the bānsurī is made any hole has to be made smaller or larger so that the notes pass the test of the ear, the baddha pañcama will remain under the maker's control. The second advantage is that if, while playing, the end of the bānsurī touches some object or the seat by mistake, the Pañcama may be disturbed, but with the baddha pañcama this disturbance is impossible. The third advantage is that if the player, by his skill, wishes to use mandra Madhyama (Ṃa) in some rāga, [he can do so] by closing the baddha pañcama with the big toe. The length of the pipe or bamboo will be 10 times its paridhimāna (measure of the inner circumference); in it, placing the mouth-hole at the first part (1/10) from the top and mandra Pañcama at the first part (1/10) from the bottom, if the other notes are placed in the remaining eight parts, it will be excellent.

following.text: One more method of making the bānsurī, simpler than the one above, is given here. I myself make [bānsurīs] by it. Its rules are set out in the following 7 ślokas
